newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo resigns.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo resigns.

text.p: Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo of Zaire, where rebels have taken over about a quarter of the country, resigned on Monday, a spokesman for his party said.
"The prime minister handed his resignation to the President (Mobutu Sese Seko)," Zola Kinkela, spokesman for the Union of Independent Democrats (UDI), told Reuters in Kinshasa.
Kengo had become the prime scapegoat for the government army's failure to stem the advance of Laurent Kabila's rebels.
The transitional parliament voted to oust Kengo and his government last week but the prime minister had earlier rejected the move as unconstitutional.
Political analysts said Kengo's decision to quit was inevitable after Mobutu effectively backed parliament's position on Monday, saying he "took note" of the anti-Kengo vote.
Zola said Kengo handed his resignation to Mobutu at 6:30 P.M. (1630 GMT).

Political parties were expected to meet quickly to designate a successor. Zaire's main opposition leader, Etienne Tshisekedi, is a likely candidate if he can agree key conditions with Mobutu, political sources said.
Under the terms of the transitional constitution, opposition parties in parliament have the right to pick the prime minister.
Kengo had been prime minister since 1994. Mobutu picked him largely because of his track record as an able administrator who enjoyed a degree of confidence among Western donors.

But Kengo was a soft target after the launch of the rebellion last October. His pledges to muster a strong defence by the army proved empty and his parenthood -- half Belgian and half Tutsi -- left him vulnerable to claims he was in league with the Tutsi-led rebels.
